sections.heading: C — Requirements for Oklahoma Drivers
sections.markdown:
## C — Requirements for Oklahoma Drivers

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
Driven cars need a current tag, registration, and title, registration at a Service Oklahoma site or licensed operator after taxes and fees buys a new tag or year sticker, buyers and sellers must transfer title there to prove ownership, and transfer fees follow vehicle age, type, and value [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
Liability means you answer legally and financially for harm your driving causes, and Oklahoma minimums run twenty-five thousand dollars, fifty thousand dollars for multi-victim injury or death, and twenty-five thousand dollars of property damage, every limit counted per accident [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
Show a current security verification form at any collision or traffic stop as supplied by the owner insurer or a non-owner policy, keep it in the car, display it to officers, Service Oklahoma staff, and fellow crash parties on demand, and copy the other side full name, license number, and birth dates for your own protection [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
Uninsured drivers and owners in a crash with any injury or five hundred dollars or more of damage lose the license to suspension, and a no-proof ticket pushes courts to notify Service Oklahoma for license plus tag suspension [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
Conviction for ignoring compulsory insurance or withholding proof from an officer or Service Oklahoma representative draws up to two hundred fifty dollars, thirty days in jail, or both, plus suspension of license and registration [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A01
Forging a security verification form risks felony conviction with fines and imprisonment, merely holding one risks a misdemeanor carrying up to two hundred fifty dollars plus mandatory suspension of driving privilege and registration, only insurer or agent issued forms count, and wise drivers confirm a current form in every car they touch since uninsured operation invites arrest and suspension [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A01
Every Service Oklahoma letter goes to your address of record, so a stale address can suspend you without your ever knowing, and keeping the license means keeping in touch [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A02
Drivers and front passengers must buckle factory belts meeting federal standards, since belts soften interior impact, hold you inside and in control, and keep buckled riders from flying forward or out [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A02
Children under eight ride only in a proper child restraint, kids at least four stay secured, restraints face rearward until age two or the maker weight and height caps, every system must meet federal crash standards, and four to eight year olds no taller than four feet nine inches use a restraint or a seat belt [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A02
Never let a child ride loose, standing, or on the floorboards, no front-seat adult can stop an infant from windshield flight, airbags have killed sub-five-foot children and elders so under-twelves belong in back, the rear seat runs twenty-six percent safer, families should settle back-seat rules at home, and buckling up is the law [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ok-d:service-oklahoma-sok:handbook:pdf-0017]
